review_type: Administrative service-driver code review only; NOT a mathematical or preprint whole-package review

findings.title: Advancing STATE before other checkpoint writes makes interruption unrecoverable
findings.counterexample: Inject OSError on CLAIM_REGISTRY.json save after STATE save. First complete raises, but STATE already includes1033 and next_pr1034. Retrying complete returns WORKFLOW_COMPLETED while registry stays PENDING and log/README never get the checkpoint.
findings.minimum_correction: Use a durable completion event, idempotently reconcile registry/log/README even for already-completed PRs, then atomically advance STATE last. Use one shared state lock for completion and other state writers, and atomic replace for JSON.

findings.title: Merge retry repeats a PR update and nests accepted text before noticing prior merge intent
findings.counterexample: PATCH succeeds; merge command fails with PR still open. First invocation leaves MERGE_INTENT. Second merge PATCHes again, embedding the first full accepted body as preserved original, then fails at existing MERGE_INTENT. Counterexample produces two accepted headers and two PATCHes for one merge request.
findings.minimum_correction: Save one stable original-body snapshot and intended acceptance payload before first write; record PATCH/ready intents and reconcile exact live readback on retry. Check unresolved MERGE_INTENT before any further PR mutation.

findings.title: Historic tracker receipt permits merge after the required DOI row changes
findings.counterexample: After track, another authorized editor deletes or changes the row. merge consumes only local TRACKER_VERIFIED and attempts external merge without any Google read; complete likewise accepts the historical receipt. Offline probe confirms zero GWS calls before merge attempt.
findings.minimum_correction: Re-resolve the intended gid and verify current header, one DOI match and exact full row immediately before merge and final completion; update observed row number if concurrent inserts moved the row.

findings.title: Exact reviewed head is accepted on an unintended base branch
findings.counterexample: Return an open same-head PR whose base.ref is other-branch. Driver performs acceptance PATCH and attempts gh pr merge; no assertion requires main. A successful merge would pass head-parent proof and completion despite reaching the wrong base.
findings.minimum_correction: Pin expected base repository and main in config; assert them on each live read and immediately before merge. Where base-retarget races matter, ensure final merged base is also checked and record it.

probe_result: Four counterexamples and three positive controls pass; all subprocess calls mocked
positive_controls: Exact-head drift blocks stage before intent/mutation
Uncertain stage with no saved ID never repeats native stage on rerun
Uncertain successful append is reconciled from exact raw row and rerun does not append
prepare_service_configs_assessment: No additional actionable finding found in narrow current-input review. Current asset digests are explicitly pinned, current final-authority paths are selected from STATE, readiness/count/zero issues are gated, and explicit scope/limitations/AI/unrefereed/UNKNOWN-priority wording is preserved. This does not recertify the seals or underlying mathematical reviews.
remaining_gap: Root fixes and independent rerun of repaired driver are required before external service execution. No external behavior was tested.
